name: Shashvat Nakrani
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded BharatPe, a fintech payments company, in March 2018 at age 19 while a third-year student at IIT Delhi, building India's first interoperable zero-MDR UPI QR code for merchants.
early_history_summary: Born in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, India, Nakrani enrolled at IIT Delhi in 2015 to study Textile Technology. He launched a startup called bookmyhaircut.com during college before co-founding BharatPe with Ashneer Grover in March 2018 at age 19. He dropped out of IIT Delhi to build the company full-time, creating an interoperable UPI QR payment system for small merchants.
family_context_summary: Father runs an education institute in Bhavnagar, Gujarat; described as a self-made educator who struggled in early years. Family supported his decision to drop out of IIT despite initial inhibitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father runs an education institute; not directly in technology or finance but provided an entrepreneurial family environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Delhi pipeline, cofounder complementarity, UPI/digital payments wave
evidence_summary: Nakrani leveraged his position at IIT Delhi, one of India's most elite engineering institutions, to meet co-founder Ashneer Grover and launch BharatPe at age 19. The company rode the massive UPI/digital payments wave in India. His father's education institute provided a modest entrepreneurial family background. The complementary cofounder relationship with Grover was critical to early execution.
starting_point: Born in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, India; father runs an education institute, middle-class entrepreneurial family.
current_position: Transitioned from executive role at BharatPe to strategic advisor and board member in 2026; estimated net worth Rs 1,300+ crore (~$160M); 19 angel investments.

trajectory.event: Co-founded BharatPe at IIT Delhi, launching India's first interoperable zero-MDR UPI QR code for merchants.

He worked briefly as a wireline field engineer at Schlumberger before co-founding Razorpay with college friend Shashank Kumar in December 2014, motivated by the dismal state of online payments in India. The company was accepted into Y Combinator and grew into India's largest payment gateway.

primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Roorkee pipeline, cofounder complementarity, digital payments wave, Y Combinator

The Y Combinator accelerator provided critical early ecosystem support. The timing aligned with India's explosive digital payments growth driven by UPI adoption.

current_position: CEO and co-founder of Razorpay; net worth approximately Rs 8,643 crore (~$1.03B) as of 2025; one of India's youngest billionaires.

He founded Insta360 in 2014 with early investment from IDG Capital.

Nanjing University provided the educational foundation, while Shenzhen's hardware ecosystem enabled manufacturing. His reputation as a technical prodigy who hacked school systems paradoxically opened doors with investors who saw rare product intuition.

early_history_summary: Born on January 16, 1988, in Padang, Indonesia, Unardi developed an interest in IT through programming competitions in high school. He graduated from high school in 2004 and moved to the US to attend Purdue University, earning BS degrees in computer science and mathematics in 2008. He worked at Microsoft for three years as a software engineer on Microsoft Lync. In 2011, he enrolled at Harvard Business School but left after one semester to co-found Traveloka in March 2012 with Derianto Kusuma and Albert Zhang, both former Microsoft colleagues.
